I am a PGY-2 (Pediatric Residency) so this is purely an opinionated post from my point of view during my training/schooling.

To be brutally honest MD programs typically take applicants with higher grades and MCAT scores. There is generally more history to allopathic medicine and it usually has more "Flair".

That begin said, a DO program does NOT mean that "all the people who couldn't get into MD programs go to DO school". That is absolutely not true. I was lucky enough to stay in California (the whole application process is a giant crap shoot) with an MD program and some of my close friends from college went to DO programs. Every program will have a spectrum of students and my friend has always told me that there's some smart ass people in her graduating class.

I'm now a resident and will say to go down the MD route if possible just to make life easier down the road even if you decide to do the "less difficult" specialties. If you do D.O. you will have to take TWO SETS OF STANDARDIZED BOARD EXAMS (USMLE and COMLEX) if you decide to apply to an allopathic residency (which I think is reason enough to prioritize MD over DO if grades aren't an issue). DOs do have their own residencies as well.

I think to help answer the question ask what you want out of life. If you want to go down one of the ROAD specialities (Radiology, Ophthalmology, Anesthesiology, Dermatology) maybe lean towards a MD program. If you want to do primary care (internal medicine, family medicine, pediatrics, OBGYN) I think DO is a perfectly fine choice.

Applying to medical school is a whole separate topic in and of itself. I've had friends who apply one year and get in on their first shot out of undergrad. Others have to apply twice to get into MD schools. I do know one guy who has applied twice now (first year no interviews, second year 1 interview) and has not gotten into a MD program. He has refused my advice to consider a DO program until this year (now his 3rd attempt).

In addition if you want to legally practice abroad you will need the MD. I was told by my friend that a DO does not satisfy the pre-req but I could be wrong.

This is a simplistic way of looking at it but will serve to be a first response until others chime in. Please PM me or respond further to here if you have further questions! :]

u/Sergipoo nailed it, but I'll sum it up to a shorter post. Ultimately, there is little difference in clinical practice of being a DO or MD. The road getting there is much more difficult for DOs though. It is easier to get into a DO school, but once you are in you have to learn more material than MDs (the osteopathic portion of medicine), you have to take 2 massive board exams instead of just one if you want to place in an MD residency (this is huge because of how stressful these tests are), and lastly, the MD vs DO discrimination is real during residency applications. For a variety of reasons, not all fair, most program directors will take an MD over a DO without a second thought.
More subjectively...which pathway interests you more? Statistics and scores mean little if you don't enjoy the curricula and lifestyle.
